items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 2, 2026
items.excerpt: Seyit Kurt 02 November 2026• Update: 02 November 2026 ISTANBUL Here's a rundown of all the news you need to start your Monday, including acting President Iliana Yotova’s victory in Bulgaria’s presidential runoff, a multi-day ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv in the Russian-controlled Ukrainian city of Oleshky ending with no violations, US President Donald Trump prioritizing diplomatic engagement with Iran despite pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to launch military strikes immediately after Tuesday's US midterm elections, and the arrest of more than 200 people in Germany following Gen Z protests. Bulgaria’s acting President Iliana Yotova was heading for a decisive victory in a presidential runoff against her pro-Western challenger, according to exit polls. Completed parallel counts by five major polling agencies put Yotova’s share of the vote at between 56.6% and 58.2% compared with 38.6% to 40.6% for Andrey Gyurov. “We accept the results, no matter how surprising they are,” Gyurov told a press conference in Sofia, adding that while the campaign is ending, the responsibility is not. Yotova, a longtime figure within the Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP), improved on her first-round result from last weekend, when she finished with 34.76% against Gyurov at 31.95%. Her campaign emphasized no additional arms support for Ukraine and instead called for peace through a diplomatic solution, in contrast to her rival. - Oleshky ceasefire between Russia, Ukraine ends with no violations reported A multi-day ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv in the Russian-controlled Ukrainian city of Oleshky ended late Sunday with no violations reported by either side. The truce, announced by US first lady Melania Trump to facilitate humanitarian aid deliveries and civilian evacuations, took effect Tuesday and was extended beyond Oleshky, in the Kherson region, to provide safe passage for humanitarian convoys. Trump said the ceasefire had given residents the freedom to move and access to food, clean water, and medicine, as well as "a renewed sense of dignity without the constant threat of attack." “Let Oleshky become the starting point for lasting peace,” she wrote on US social media platform X. - Trump favors diplomacy with Iran as Netanyahu urges strikes immediately after Tuesday's US midterms: Report US President Donald Trump is prioritizing diplomatic engagement with Iran despite pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to launch military strikes immediately after Tuesday's US midterm elections, the Axios news site reported Sunday. In a phone conversation Saturday, the Israeli leader pressed Washington to resume military action against Iran shortly after the ballot, but Trump favored allowing ongoing diplomatic tracks to play out, according to American and Israeli sources familiar with the exchange. Netanyahu is concerned about Trump’s approach, according to sources. An Israeli source characterized the discussion as "tough," while a US source described it as "direct." Trump confirmed Sunday that he had spoken with Netanyahu by phone, describing the conversation as “a very good talk.” He said the two discussed Iran but offered no further details. - More than 200 arrests in Germany after Gen Z protests German police arrested more than 200 people after violent clashes erupted in several cities following largely peaceful Generation Z demonstrations demanding better education funding and social policies. The unrest broke out in Hamburg, Frankfurt and Berlin after radical groups staged smaller demonstrations, erecting barricades and clashing with police. The main daytime demonstrations, organized by the Gen Z Regelt initiative across more than 30 cities, brought tens of thousands of young people into the streets to demand greater investment in education, action to ease the rising cost of living and an end to plans to reinstate compulsory military service. After dark, radical groups staged smaller demonstrations in other parts of the cities, erecting barricades as the situation escalated once police moved to contain them. Some activists threw stones, bottles and firecrackers at officers, who responded with water cannons and special units in several locations. ... - Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 world champion with 3rd-place finish in Mexico Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli became the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, securing the 2026 drivers' title with a third-place finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix. The 20-year-old Italian, who replaced seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes in 2025, claimed his maiden championship in only his second Formula 1 season, with four rounds remaining. Antonelli broke Sebastian Vettel's record as the youngest Formula 1 world champion and became the first Italian to win the drivers' title since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the 71-lap race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, while Ferrari's Hamilton finished second ahead of Antonelli.

items.excerpt: 1. Hormuz Talks Advance As Military Threats Persist (Diplomacy) 2. Israel Faces Coalition Deadlock After Election (Politics) 3. UN Ends Western Sahara Mission After 35 Years (Africa) 4. Ukraine Resumes Strikes On Russian Refineries (Conflict) 5. US Proposes Return Of Russian Gas To Europe (Europe) 6. Canada And US Signal Progress Towards Trade Deal (Diplomacy) 7. ... 8. ... 9. German Youth Protests Erupt Into Violence (Europe) ... Qatari mediated talks between Iran and the United States have entered a third day, with negotiators discussing a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days of an agreement. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that discussions were continuing but no final conclusion had been reached. The proposal shortens an earlier seven day timetable, although major disagreements remain over which side must act first. Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei has demanded an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions waivers, the release of frozen assets and an end to fighting on regional fronts before normal transit resumes. The diplomatic effort comes amid renewed military warnings. US President Donald Trump has ruled out fresh strikes before Tuesday’s midterm elections but not afterwards. Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered military readiness, while tanker attacks continue around Hormuz, leaving global oil supplies exposed to further disruption. Israel faces difficult coalition negotiations after last week’s election left neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with a parliamentary majority. Netanyahu’s bloc secured 53 seats, against 48 for Eisenkot’s allies, while Arab parties won 19 in the 120-member Knesset. Both leaders had ruled out working with them before the vote. President Isaac Herzog, who will begin consultations with parties on Wednesday, has urged politicians to approach negotiations with an open heart and find creative solutions to avoid another election. Eisenkot has since indicated willingness to work with representatives who accept four conditions covering Israeli sovereignty, military service and opposition to Hamas. Netanyahu continues to reject cooperation with Arab parties. Alternative routes also face obstacles. Netanyahu could seek defectors from the opposition or a unity government with Eisenkot but longstanding political disputes complicate both options. Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister while coalition talks proceed. The United Nations has ended its 35 year peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara after Russia and the United States failed to agree on its future. Russia vetoed a US resolution supporting Moroccan sovereignty over the disputed territory, while a rival Russian proposal to extend the mission failed to secure sufficient votes. ... Established in 1991, the mission monitored a ceasefire between Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front and was intended to facilitate a referendum on ... Morocco welcomed the mission’s closure, while the Polisario and its principal backer, Algeria, condemned the decision. ... Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries despite pressure from US President Donald Trump’s administration to halt attacks on energy infrastructure. Russian authorities reported a major drone attack on an industrial facility in the Nizhny Novgorod region, amid reports that the Kstovo refinery was hit. Another refinery in Samara was struck on Friday. Ukrainian officials denied agreeing to a 30 day pause requested by Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner. The White House has blamed Ukrainian refinery attacks for rising global fuel prices, while Trump lifted US sanctions on Russian diesel last month. Kyiv has targeted Russian energy facilities to weaken the country’s war economy. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported extensive Russian strikes on Ukraine’s electricity infrastructure, leaving hundreds of thousands of households without power.

items.title: U.S. Economy Grows 3.4% as 3.7% Inflation Keeps Costs in Focus | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: By Adrian Vale Nov 2, 2026, 4:15 AM UTC Updated Nov 2, 2026, 4:15 AM UTC 3 min read ... The U.S. economy expanded at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, while inflation reached 3.7% over the year through September as voters prepared to weigh economic conditions in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Gallup found that 50% of registered voters surveyed Oct. 1-19 viewed the economy as extremely important to their congressional vote; 42% said the same of gas prices. In a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted Aug. 28-31, 47% selected cost of living as the single most important factor in their midterm vote. A September AP-NORC survey of 2,140 adults found 17% approved of President Donald Trump’s handling of cost of living and 26% approved of his handling of the economy. The poll’s margin of sampling error was 2.9 percentage points. The Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) estimated real gross domestic product (GDP) grew at a 3.4% annual rate from July through September, compared with 2.2% in the second quarter. Investment, consumer spending and government spending contributed to the gain; lower exports partly offset it as imports increased. BEA data show real personal consumption expenditures grew at a 3.8% annual rate. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.6% in September from August and 3.7% over the 12 months through September. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3% for the month and 2.6% over the year. The CPI gasoline index climbed 9.1% in September, accounting for more than half of that month’s increase in the overall index. Annual inflation had fallen from 9.1% in June 2022 to 2.3% in April 2025 before rising again; the lower rate meant prices were rising more slowly, not falling overall. The Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October, from 84.2 in September. The board said confidence remained on a long-term downward trend and consumers planned to reduce spending on services and durable goods over the next six months. Its six-month moving average rose only among consumers younger than 35 and households with incomes of $100,000 or more. Fergus McCormick, a senior economist for Global Indicators at The Conference Board, said consumers “continued to express frustration with rising costs.” AAA’s national averages on Nov. 1 were $4.1732 per gallon for regular gasoline and $6.3039 for diesel, compared with $3.0380 and $3.6862 a year earlier. Freddie Mac reported a 7.24% average rate for a 30-year fixed mortgage on Oct. 29, up from 6.17% on Oct. 30, 2025. The Federal Reserve raised its target range for the federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point in September, then held it at 3.75%-4.00% on Oct. 28; two members favored another increase at that meeting. The S&P 500 closed at 7,580.07 on Oct. 30, below its 7,818.93 close on Oct. 6 but about 10.7% above its Dec. 31, 2025, close of 6,845.50. The next scheduled readings are October CPI on Nov. 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET and the second estimate of third-quarter GDP on Nov. 25 at 8:30 a.m. ET. The Federal Reserve’s next meeting is Dec. 8-9.

items.title: Oil prices fall as Iran-U.S pursue diplomacy
items.excerpt: crude falls below $100 amid reports of U.S.-Iran diplomatic efforts Published Mon, Nov 2 2026 12:04 AM EST Updated 3 Min Ago Justina Lee@in/justina-lee-2742aa59 Key Points - U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that Trump prefers not to use military force and would like to resolve the Iranian war "diplomatically." - Iranian authorities also signaled that a deal is still possible, following two days of talks mediated by Qatar, as long as demands are implemented tangibly, according to Al Jazeera. - However, concerns over the Middle East and Ukraine conflicts will likely linger in the near term. ... Oil prices fell sharply early on Monday amid reports that both the U.S. and Iran are seeking diplomatic options to bring an end to the Middle East conflict. Futures for international benchmark Brent crude Add To Watchlist for January delivery fell 3.91% to $109.00 a barrel as of 4:07 a.m. ET. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures Add To Watchlist for December declined 4.1% to $99.85 per barrel. Brent U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that President Donald Trump prefers not to use military force and would like to resolve the Iranian war "diplomatically." Trump "hasn't made a decision...what the president expresses to you is incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it, and we really we have everything we need to be successful. But we would prefer to do it peacefully," Rubio said, speaking to reporters over the weekend. Iranian authorities also signaled that a deal is still possible, following two days of talks mediated by Qatar, as long as demands are implemented tangibly, according to Al Jazeera.

items.title: US economy under Donald Trump in five charts | The National
items.excerpt: Kyle Fitzgerald Washington November 02, 2026 A nervous US electorate is heading to polling stations across the country for Tuesday's midterm elections, and their personal finances could determine which way control in Congress swings. Recent polling suggests President Donald Trump's shifting tariff policies, war with Iran and overall handling of the economy will be major issues this week for voters, who say they have been affected by higher prices at the petrol pumps and on grocery shelves. Half of registered voters rate the economy as “extremely important this year”, with health care costs and the war in Iran also top among 11 issues rated in an October 29 Gallup poll. Roughly four in 10 voters rate income and wealth distribution (44 per cent) and petrol costs (42 per cent) as extremely important. Forty-seven per cent of registered voters said the cost of living would be the single most important ... Easing petrol prices saw some recovery in the Consumer Confidence Index, which rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October, although confidence remains on a long-term and persistent downwards trend. Moreover, consumers are planning for less spending on services and goods over the next six months, reflecting enduring inflation. Despite this anxiety, consumer spending rose at a 3.4 per cent pace in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department data, showing the US economy has remained resilient amid the energy price shock caused by the Iran war. Strong business spending also accounted for US GDP to grow at a 3.4 per cent annual pace in the July to September period. US inflation has significantly eased since peaking at 9.1 per cent in 2022, and fell to 3 per cent when Mr Trump began his second term in office in January 2025. Headline inflation fell as low as 2.3 per cent in April that year. But inflation picked up again after he imposed a sweeping set of tariffs on nearly every trading partner. The disinflation process now appears stalled, and the Iran war has led to surging energy prices couple with AI-driven investment. Petrol prices accounted for nearly half of the all-items increase in September, when CPI inflation clocked in at 3.7 per cent. Even after stripping away food and energy, inflation still gained 0.3 per cent on a monthly basis and 2.6 per cent year on year. It has been nearly six years since CPI inflation registered at 2 per cent. Seventy-nine per cent of Americans agreed that prices at the pump were higher now compared to 38 per cent in February, a dramatic shift in perceptions since the Iran war began, according to an Ipsos poll conducted in September. The prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the world's energy supplies, has pushed up global energy costs. Even the US, the world's top crude producer, has not been fully insulated. Ukrainian strikes against Russian refineries have exacerbated rising costs for diesel, which powers the lorries that transport food and other goods. The average driver is currently paying $4.20 for a gallon of petrol today, an increase of $1.17 from the same time last year, according to automotive group AAA. Of the six “swing states” in this year's midterm election cycle, only Georgia's petrol prices are below the national average. Diesel prices have also soared to $6.32, compared to $3.68 a gallon a year ago.

items.title: Dollar Index Holds Near 102 as Inflation and Iran Diplomacy Shape Trading | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: By Adrian Vale Nov 2, 2026, 4:27 AM UTC ... The U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) was near 102 in Asian trading Monday, FXStreet reported, as September inflation and Iran diplomacy shaped competing pressures on the U.S. currency. FXStreet said waning demand for the dollar’s safe-haven role was restraining it; the outlet also cited inflation and rate-hike expectations as offsetting forces. Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) says the index compares the dollar with six currencies through a real-time geometric calculation. The Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported that the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.5% from August and 3.6% from a year earlier in September, compared with increases of 0.3% and 3.4% in August. Core PCE advanced 0.3% month over month and 3.1% year over year, after increases of 0.3% and 3.0% in August. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% on Oct. 28. The 10-2 vote included two officials who favored a 0.25-percentage-point increase. The committee said, “Inflation remains elevated.” FXStreet reported roughly 75% odds of a December increase, citing CME FedWatch. CME says its probabilities are implied by 30-Day Federal Funds futures prices.

items.title: Trump makes final weekend campaign push ahead of midterm elections
items.excerpt: In the last weekend before the pivotal midterm elections, US President Donald Trump has made a ... Trump held rallies in Florida, Iowa and Kansas - states he won in past elections - in a sign of Republicans' defensive stance ahead of Tuesday's vote. Facing voter frustration over rising prices, Trump sought to tamp down such concerns and shift focus on attacking Democrats, saying they would "bankrupt" families if elected. Polls suggest that Democrats have a good chance at winning at least partial control of Congress, which would act as a check on Trump's power and could upend the last two years of his presidency. ... Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries said this weekend that he was "very confident" his party was on course to win control of the House of Representatives, as senior Democrats including former President Barack Obama made final appeals to voters. A forecasting tool from Harvard University that analyses and compiles multiple polls and historical data suggests that Democrats have a 96% chance of taking the House and a 76% chance of taking the Senate. A national poll from NBC News posted this weekend suggests that registered voters prefer a Democrat-controlled Congress by a 7-point margin, leading Republicans 52% to 45%.

items.title: US midterms: 1 day to go – Democrats rally around El-Sayed amid attacks | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
items.excerpt: With one day to go before the United States midterm elections, campaigning has reached a fever pitch with Democratic and Republican leaders pulling out all the stops to mobilise voters. Democrats are hoping to flip control of both chambers of Congress, which is currently controlled by US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the Senate’s 100 seats are up for grabs on Tuesday. Voting will also be held to elect governors in 36 of the 50 US states. With the cost-of-living crisis, exacerbated by the US-Israel war on Iran, becoming one of the key talking points of these elections, here’s where things stand as of Monday: ## What’s happened on the campaign trail in the past 24 hours? In a dramatic political development on Sunday, Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens threw her support behind Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers over her own party’s nominee, Abdul El-Sayed, in Michigan – one of the most closely watched races of the US midterm elections. Stevens had lost Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary in August to El-Sayed. Her announcement followed weeks of tension with El-Sayed over US support to Israel, which has been accused of committing genocide in Gaza. El-Sayed has opposed military support to Israel, arguing that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pushed the US into the Iran war. Stevens has accused El-Sayed of anti-Semitism for his criticism of Israeli actions in Gaza. El-Sayed said a vote for his rival Rogers “is going to be a vote for Donald Trump” as his campaign reportedly saw a fundraising surge after Stevens crossed party lines. Democratic leaders have rallied behind El-Sayed, who has faced Islamophobic attacks during the campaign. The chairman of the Democratic Party in Michigan criticised Stevens. “She does not speak for that larger community,” Curtis Hertel said in an interview with CNN. The leader of the Democrats in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, slammed Stevens over her endorsement of the Republican candidate. “This is a despicable betrayal from Representative Stevens,” he posted on X. “Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors.” Meanwhile, the advocacy group Michigan Jews for Democracy has backed El-Sayed. “Haley Stevens does not speak for Michigan’s Jewish community,” it said in a statement, which rejected her “attempt to divide our community” two days before the election. While Democrats have been angered by Stevens’s action, Trump celebrated her decision. During a rally in Iowa later on Sunday, the US president said he would “love” it if Stevens joined the Republican Party. “Haley said what few people are willing to say,” Trump added. “It’s a thing called bravery.” The question now is whether Stevens’s endorsement could persuade some of her supporters to back Rogers or discourage them from voting altogether. Polling suggested El-Sayed has largely consolidated Democratic support, according to the Reuters news agency.

items.excerpt: Judge dismisses lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska Senate race if GOP incumbent loses JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — A federal judge on Sunday dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska’s U.S. Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses, the latest development in a ballot controversy that has roiled the final days of one of the nation’s most closely watched races. Sullivan, an ally of President Donald Trump, faces Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman, in a race that is among a handful expected to determine which party controls the Senate for the final two years of Trump's term. Tuesday’s ranked-choice election also includes two candidates who have done little campaigning, one of whom shares the incumbent’s name. It was that candidate's presence on the ballot that prompted Trump to push for the lawsuit out of fear he would siphon votes from the incumbent. Shortly after the ruling, the Justice Department filed a notice that it would appeal: “Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes,” a department spokesperson said in a statement. The lawsuit, filed less than two weeks before the election and as early voting was underway, called for an investigation into whether votes for retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan were intended for the senator. The state said the case lacked merit and argued there would be no way to determine that without violating voter privacy. Analysis: Republicans face a midterm reckoning of Trump's making WASHINGTON (AP) — For President Donald Trump, this week's elections are about him. For his fellow Republicans, the risk is voters will agree. Midterms almost always serve as a referendum on the president’s party, and losses typically ensue. But Trump’s decisions to impose tariffs, start a war and oversee extravagant Washington renovations — largely without congressional consultation — have made it harder for Republicans to navigate those historical headwinds. There is a direct connection between his actions and higher gas prices, costlier groceries and persistently high inflation. Republicans cannot blame the fallout from those decisions on past administrations when Trump has owned them so fulsomely. They also cannot easily distance themselves from an unpopular president who demands loyalty and routinely tells voters the economy is just fine. At virtually every juncture before Election Day on Tuesday, Trump has complicated the task of protecting Republican majorities in Congress.

items.title: Anirudh exits Shah Rukh Khan's King, Sachin-Jigar take over music duties - India Today
items.excerpt: New Delhi, Nov 2, 2026 10:42 IST It's now clear that Shah Rukh Khan's King has a new musical team. Composer-singer Anirudh has reportedly stepped away from the film because of his packed schedule. However, he isn't leaving the project entirely empty-handed. He's said to have given Shah Rukh a theme track as a mark of respect for the actor, even as composer-duo Sachin-Jigar take charge of the film's songs and background score. According to a report by Bollywood Hungama, Anirudh and the makers mutually decided to part ways after his commitments in the South made it difficult for him to give the film the time it needed. With Shah Rukh and director Siddharth Anand keen to bring King to cinemas this Christmas without delays, the team reportedly decided to make the change. ... The decision to part ways from the project was reportedly amicable, with Sachin-Jigar now handling the album as well as the background score. Anirudh, meanwhile, has composed the film's theme track, which will continue to feature in the project. The source further revealed, "Anirudh has given the theme track of King to Shah Rukh Khan as a mark of his respect for the megastar, and Sachin-Jigar too will be reimagining the track for the entire background score of the film. So King will still have the Anirudh touch with the theme track, but the entire score and the album will be done by Sachin-Jigar." ### SRK- Deepika Padukone's Tu Mil Jaaye releases The timing is interesting, as King has just begun unveiling its music. Shah Rukh marked his birthday on November 2 with the midnight release of Tu Mil Jaaye, the film's first song, which features him alongside Deepika Padukone. The track has received mixed reactions. While Arijit Singh's vocals, the melody and Shah Rukh and Deepika's chemistry have found appreciation, some listeners have questioned its familiar sound, visuals, editing and styling. ... Composed by Sachin-Jigar, Tu Mil Jaaye features vocals by Arijit Singh and Madhubanti Bagchi, with Sheeran performing the English rap. The romantic track also brings Shah Rukh and Deepika together on screen once again.

items.excerpt: ## A2O LITE Win ‘Inkigayo’ for a Second Straight Week, Their 8th Music-Show Trophy A2O LITE won No. 1 on SBS’s “Inkigayo” on Nov. 1 with their debut single “NEON,” scoring 6,576 points ahead of NMIXX’s “Birthday Wish” (4,047) and IVE’s “Looks Can Kill” (3,735). It is their second “Inkigayo” trophy in a row and their eighth music-show win overall, all collected in the 13 days since their first win on “The Show” on Oct. 20, across six different programs. “We’re so happy and grateful to receive such a precious award again this week,” the group said on stage, thanking A2O Entertainment founder Lee Soo-man. “NEON” was still No. 1 on the Melon TOP100 at 4 a.m. KST on Nov. 2, and SBS’s official stage video reached 974,329 views in about 13 hours. Eight trophies less than three weeks after debut: a hook that started as a meme is now the song the whole country is dancing to. Sources: Top Star News, Nov. 1, Ilgan Sports, Nov. 1, Melon TOP100 (checked 4 a.m. KST, Nov. 2), YouTube views checked 5 a.m. KST, Nov. 2 ## BTS Close the Latin American Leg of the ‘ARIRANG’ Tour in São Paulo BTS wrapped up the Latin American leg of their “ARIRANG” world tour with three sold-out concerts at São Paulo’s MorumBIS stadium on Oct. 28, 30 and 31 (local time), and the tour continues in Asia with Kaohsiung, Taiwan, in November. Brazilian media had expected about 90,000 fans a night, and the tour as a whole spans 79 shows in 34 regions, the biggest in the group’s history. Back home, the album “ARIRANG” spent its 31st straight week on the Billboard 200 (No. 46 on the chart dated Oct. 31), and Jin’s solo songs “Don’t Say You Love Me” and “To Me, Today” played as the soundtrack of the Seoul Arts Center’s World Music Fountain through Nov. 1. Seven years after their last stadium shows in Brazil, ARMY there finally got their reunion, and Asia is next in line. ... ## IVE’s ‘Looks Can Kill’ Sells 714,887 Copies in Its First Week IVE’s fifth mini album “Looks Can Kill” sold 714,887 copies in its first week, according to Hanteo Chart figures reported Nov. 1. That is 47,653 more (up 7.14%) than February’s second full album “REVIVE+” (667,234), and the first time since October 2023 that an IVE album has outsold the one before it in week one. The title track has climbed as high as No. 6 on Melon’s daily chart and was No. 7 on the Melon TOP100 at 4 a.m. KST on Nov. 2, and the group performed it again on “Inkigayo” on Nov. 1. Turning the numbers back upward in their fifth year is exactly the kind of quiet strength DIVE have always believed in. Sources: Sports Kyunghyang, Nov. 1, Melon TOP100 (checked 4 a.m. KST, Nov. 2)
